_doc: Story 4.4 GOLDEN FIXTURE — the ACCEPTED-PRICE DELTA SHAPE pin (4.4-GOLDEN-01, R-410; feeds Epic 7). Pins the fixture SHAPE ONLY for an accepted (frozen) price vs a later recalculated price: each case carries the accepted total öre, a later recalculated total öre, and the delta öre = recalculated - accepted, plus an `origin` label + a `note` documenting the delta semantics. This is a FIXTURE-SHAPE deliverable ONLY — Epic 4 supplies the golden 'accepted price vs later recalculated price' delta SHAPE; enforcement of accepted-state IMMUTABILITY / new-version-on-change lives in Epic 6/7 (this fixture builds NO acceptance/immutability code, NO table, NO persistence). The EXACT accepted-price-delta representation is an OPEN owner/design question (Sign-Off Q8) — the shapes below are DEFENSIBLE pilot assumptions labelled as such, NOT Epic-7-final. The delta arithmetic is a LIVE oracle: the golden-pack test recomputes delta = recalculatedTotalOre - acceptedTotalOre via plain integer arithmetic / `sumOre` on the fixture öre (no new engine surface), so a mis-stated delta fails LOUD. Where a genuine OLD-LOVABLE number is known from the anonymized behavioral oracle (Lovable's round-at-end / hardcoded-25% gross shortcut), it is captured as an `old-lovable`-labelled accepted total OR a `documented-delta` carrying BOTH the Lovable value (`oldLovableWouldGive`) and the new-expected value + why they diverge — NEVER Lovable code or real Lovable data (behavioral-oracle-only rule). Money/öre numbers ONLY — NO PII (personnummer/orgnr/name/email/phone/address), NO clock (NFR17/R-411). STOP (needs-human) if the accepted-price-delta representation must be treated as production-approved (Sign-Off Q8) or if real customer quote data is needed to produce a fixture.

policy.deltaFormula: deltaOre = recalculatedTotalOre - acceptedTotalOre (a POSITIVE delta = the recalculated price is HIGHER than the accepted/frozen one; NEGATIVE = lower; zero = unchanged)
policy.acceptedTotal: the FROZEN accepted total öre — Epic 6/7 owns the immutability of this value; Epic 4 pins the delta SHAPE only, it does NOT freeze or persist anything
policy.recalculatedTotal: a LATER recalculated total öre (e.g. after a settings/rate/price change) — computed by the SAME 4.1/4.2/4.3 engine; the delta is the customer-visible price movement Epic 7 will gate
policy.epic7Boundary: new-version-on-change / accepted-state immutability enforcement is EPIC 7 — this fixture supplies ONLY the golden delta SHAPE (no acceptance table, no immutability code)
policy.signOffQ8: the exact accepted-price-delta representation is OPEN (Sign-Off Q8) — the shapes here are pilot assumptions, not Epic-7-final

deltaCases.note: The baseline: a recalculation with NO input change reproduces the accepted total EXACTLY -> delta 0 öre. The accepted total 100000 öre and the recalculated total 100000 öre are identical (the engine is deterministic; re-running the same inputs yields the same öre). A non-zero delta here would signal a non-deterministic engine and fail loud.

A later recalculation AFTER a customer-visible change yields a HIGHER total -> positive delta. Accepted (frozen) total 100000 öre; after a change the recalculated total is 112500 öre -> delta = 112500 - 100000 = +12500 öre. Epic 7 will require a NEW quote version for this customer-visible movement; Epic 4 pins ONLY the delta shape (no enforcement).

A later recalculation yields a LOWER total -> negative delta. Accepted 112500 öre; recalculated 100000 öre -> delta = 100000 - 112500 = -12500 öre. A negative delta is a valid signed shape (the accepted price was higher than the later recalculation); Epic 7 owns whether this needs a new version.

DOCUMENTED divergence from Lovable's round-at-end behaviour (R-403 / R-410). Three lines of (0.5 x 45 = 22.5 -> 23 öre each). The NEW engine freezes the accepted total via sum-of-rounded = 23*3 = 69 öre. Lovable's implicit round-at-end would have frozen Math.round(67.5) = 68 öre (captured as an anonymized behavioral-oracle number, NOT copied code/data). So an accepted total frozen under the OLD Lovable rule (68) vs a total recalculated under the NEW sum-of-rounded engine (69) shows delta = 69 - 68 = +1 öre — the intentional, documented migration delta. This is why the labelling matters: the 1-öre movement is EXPLAINABLE (round-at-end -> sum-of-rounded), not an unexplained diff.

DOCUMENTED OLD-LOVABLE behaviour captured as an anonymized number (behavioral-oracle-only; NO Lovable code/data). Lovable computed a customer-facing gross via a hardcoded 25% VAT shortcut (net x 1.25, round-at-end). For an accepted net of 85000 öre Lovable's frozen gross was round(85000 x 1.25) = 106250 öre. The NEW basis-point engine recomputes the SAME accepted line via vatBreakdown(85000, 2500) -> gross 106250 öre (net 85000 + per-line VAT round(85000*2500/10000)=21250). Here the two AGREE (delta 0) because the net is exact under 25%; the `old-lovable` label records that this frozen value ORIGINATES from Lovable's hardcoded-25% behaviour, so a future rate change (e.g. the customer was actually at 12%) would surface an EXPLAINABLE delta pointing at the hardcoded-25% assumption rather than an unexplained diff.

_transactionDoc: Story 7.2 EXTENSION (7.2-GOLDEN-01, R-705/R-717) — the ACCEPTED-QUOTE-TO-JOB TRANSACTION SHAPE. This block is ADDITIVE and DISTINCT from `deltaCases`: `deltaCases` pins the 4.4 accepted-vs-LATER-RECALCULATED movement (feeds the new-version-on-change concept); `transactionCases` pins Epic 7 R-705's adjusted-price = accepted-price-VS-SENT-TOTAL-AT-ACCEPTANCE-TIME plus the transaction's immutable SOURCE REFERENCES (accepted version id + acceptance id → job) and the öre totals persisted on the acceptance/job. Do NOT conflate the two deltas. Each case carries the frozen source sent total öre, the accepted price öre, the transaction delta öre = acceptedPriceOre - sourceSentTotalOre, a `reasonRequired` flag (any non-zero delta REQUIRES a reason/evidence — the AC5 gate the transaction re-enforces), and the shape of the created job's source refs (label-only placeholders — NO real ids, this is a SHAPE pin). Money/öre numbers ONLY, all < 10 digits (R-717) — NO PII (personnummer/orgnr/name/email/phone/address), NO clock (NFR17/R-411). The documented Lovable transactional delta is LABELLED (Lovable's mutable-acceptance / client-side-multi-step vs Phase A's immutable single-transaction) — NEVER Lovable code/data; only `new-expected` + one `documented-delta` case, no fabricated oracle. POLICY STATUS: pilot assumptions, Sign-Off Q8 open; nothing production-approved.

transactionPolicy.transactionDeltaFormula: transactionDeltaOre = acceptedPriceOre - sourceSentTotalOre (POSITIVE = accepted above the sent total; NEGATIVE = below; zero = unchanged). This is the ACCEPTANCE-TIME adjusted-price delta (R-705), NOT the 4.4 accepted-vs-recalculated delta.
transactionPolicy.reasonRequiredRule: reasonRequired = transactionDeltaOre !== 0 — the AC5 gate the acceptQuoteAndCreateJob transaction re-validates server-side (the client cannot bypass).
transactionPolicy.sourceRefs: the created job stores the accepted quote_version_id + quote_acceptance_id as IMMUTABLE source references (composite same-tenant FKs, ON DELETE RESTRICT). The fixture pins the SHAPE (which refs exist), not real ids.
transactionPolicy.distinctFrom44: 4.4 `deltaCases` = accepted-vs-later-recalculated; 7.2 `transactionCases` = accepted-price-vs-sent-total-at-acceptance-time + source refs. Related shape, different semantics — do not merge.
transactionPolicy.signOffQ8: the exact accepted-price-delta representation is OPEN (Sign-Off Q8) — pilot assumptions, not Epic-7-final

transactionCases.note: The unchanged case (AC1 happy path): the accepted price EQUALS the frozen source sent total -> transaction delta 0 öre -> NO adjustment reason required. The transaction records the acceptance (accepted_price_ore = source_sent_total_ore = 125000), flips the version sent->accepted, and creates ONE job whose source refs point at the accepted version + the acceptance. A non-zero delta here would wrongly demand a reason and fail loud.

The adjusted case (AC5): the accepted price is BELOW the frozen source sent total (a documented customer discount) -> transaction delta -5000 öre -> a reason/evidence IS required. accepted 120000 - sent 125000 = -5000. The transaction persists the accepted price AS GIVEN (R-716 — no VAT/ROT re-derivation) alongside the frozen source total; both are immutable commitment data (7.4 locks them).

The adjusted case (AC5), positive direction: the accepted price is ABOVE the frozen source sent total (a documented scope add) -> transaction delta +2000 öre -> a reason/evidence IS required. accepted 127000 - sent 125000 = +2000. Proves the signed delta shape and that the reason gate fires in BOTH directions.

DOCUMENTED behavioral divergence from Lovable (behavioral-oracle-only; NO Lovable code/data). Lovable recorded acceptance as a MUTABLE, client-side MULTI-STEP sequence (an acceptance row, then a separately-created job) with no single-transaction guarantee — a retry/double-submit could fork the customer commitment (two jobs) or leave a half-accepted quote. Phase A replaces this with ONE immutable atomic transaction whose accepted price + source refs are frozen. The `documented-delta` here is BEHAVIORAL, not numeric: `oldLovableWouldGive` records the mutable/forkable Lovable outcome shape; `newExpected` records the single-immutable-transaction outcome. The öre values match the unchanged case (125000) — the divergence is the TRANSACTION SEMANTICS (mutable-multi-step vs immutable-single-transaction), which is why 7.2's idempotency/atomicity INT proofs, not a number, are the enforcement.
transactionCases.oldLovableWouldGive: mutable client-side multi-step acceptance-then-job (forkable on retry: two jobs / half-accepted quote)
transactionCases.newExpected: one immutable atomic idempotent transaction (retry/concurrent-accept returns the existing single acceptance + job)
